title: Cancer Control Research Program
text: CANCER CONTROL RESEARCH PROGRAM The Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center (Sylvester) Cancer Control (CC) Research Program is coled by Frank J. Penedo, PhD, and Tracy E. Crane, PhD, who offer complementary expertise across the cancer control continuum from prevention to survivorship. CC advances cancer control science throughout Sylvesterfs four-county catchment area (CA). These efforts strategically align with the programfs two specific aims 1) identify and characterize multilevel determinants of cancer etiology, risk, and outcomes from prevention to survivorship; and 2) design and test innovative interventions to reduce gaps in cancer care and improve outcomes across the cancer control continuum. With Sylvester investments, CC has continued to mature, growing in membership, scientific productivity, and scope in alignment with Sylvesterfs 2019-2023 Strategic Plan. Targeted faculty recruitment has added expertise in social epidemiology, cancer care delivery, cancer survivorship, and lifestyle medicine (health behavior) research. The program has achieved key milestones including receiving a Training to Reduce Burden across the Cancer Control Continuum (TRACC) T32 training grant, creating a Hispanic/Latino(a) (H/L) cancer survivorship cohort, and launching several transdisciplinary, multisite, and innovative CA-relevant projects. CC has grown to include 47 members from four University of Miami Colleges and Schools (Schools of Medicine, Music, Communications, and the College of Arts and Sciences), representing 12 departments. CC has $7.4M in annual direct peer-reviewed, cancerrelated extramural funding.an increase of over $1M annually since the prior submission, including $2.9M from the National Cancer Institute (NCI). Over the reporting period (6/1/2018- 5/31/2023), program members published 817 peerreviewed, cancer-relevant papers; 24% (n=200) were intra-programmatic and 15% (n=126) inter-programmatic, 18% (n=144) were in journals with impact factors .10, and 73% (n=599) were published with collaborators from other institutions. Support for faculty recruits totaled $11.8M and Sylvester Intramural Funding Program (IFP) investments of $2.1M to CC members resulted in $6.9M of external funding, over a 3- fold return on investment. Grounded in Sylvesterfs unique CA, CC has characterized a greater appreciation of the critical heterogeneity of cancer risk, prevalence, and outcomes and developed novel interventions that have led to practice-changing impact across the cancer continuum. Sylvesterfs investments in key research infrastructure, most notably the Behavioral and Community-Based Research Shared Resource, and Sylvesterfs Office of Outreach and Engagement ensure input from key community stakeholders to address community priorities in cancer control. CC continues to develop a highly collaborative and engaged membership that forms a robust, sustainable, and comprehensive program that advances Sylvesterfs mission among vulnerable populations in SoFL and beyond.

title: Exploring new approaches for enhanced human gene annotation
text:
Identifying the genes that are active in a cell is a critical step in studying cell development,
genetic diseases, responses to infection, the effects of mutations, and much more. During the
last decade, high-throughput RNA-sequencing data have proven essential to characterizing the
genes expressed in different cell types and conditions, which in turn has driven a strong demand
for highly efficient, scalable, and accurate computational methods to process these data. This
project will design and implement new algorithms to process the ever-growing and diverse types
of RNA-sequencing experiments in order to produce more accurate human gene and transcript
annotation.

title: Radiation and dendritic cells to hepatomas to improve immunotherapy response
text:
Patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma have poor overall survival. Immunotherapy with PD-L1
and VEGF inhibitor is a recent major advance, however, progression free survival remains short at less than 7
months. We propose to examine the clinical activities and immune effect of a novel combination therapy using
radiation followed by intratumor injection of autologous dendritic cells followed by standard of care PD-L1 and
VEGF inhibitors.

title: How do astrocytes regulate neuronal circuits?
text:
While the electrical activity of neurons is thought of as the basis of our thoughts, memories, and
actions, the brain is also composed of an array of support cells that can actively control
neuronal firing and an organism’s behavior. Thus, in order to understand how the brain forms
neuronal circuits and why those circuits are disrupted in disease, we must understand how
these support cells can control neuronal activity. This proposal focuses on decoding which
signals these support cells respond to and how they change the electrical activity of the brain in
order to understand how the brain normally functions and how these support cells may change
brain function in disease and injury.

title: Translational big data analytic approaches to advance drug repurposing for Alzheimer's disease
text:
Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a major public health crisis with no available cure. We propose innovative
translational big data analytic methods to improve our understanding of the genetic, molecular and
neurobiological mechanisms of AD, facilitate the identification of novel promising targets and drugs for
repurposing, and ultimately have a translational impact on disease treatment and prevention. The resulting
methods are also expected to impact biomedical research in general and benefit public health outcomes.

title: Modeling and dynamics of biomolecules on cellular scales
text:
Most biological function takes place inside cells. This research aims at understanding the
fundamental principles at the molecular level for how cellular environments shape
biological function and disease. Understanding how cellular environments alter
biomolecular behavior will furthermore inform more effective rational design strategies to
identify new therapies targeting a variety of diseases.

title: Monoclonal Antibody Cocktail for Treatment of Marburg Virus Disease
text:
Filoviruses are among the deadliest pathogens known to humans. The Ebola virus disease outbreak in West
Africa (2014-2016), caused by the Zaire Ebola virus, resulted in over 28,000 cases and 11,000 deaths. In addition
to Ebola virus, a related filovirus called Marburg has caused five outbreaks in the past 10 years with high fatality
rates. This proposal is aimed at developing effective immunoprotherapeutic against Marburg virus for protection
against Marburg virus disease. We have generated several antibody drug candidates that protect against
Marburg infection. Under this proposal we will engineer two lead antibody to acquire long term durability after
injection and we will perform animal efficacy studies with a cocktail of these antibodies. This study, if successful,
will set the stage for clinical development of an effective therapeutic for human use.

title: Characterizing, optimizing, and harmonizing cancer detection with PET imaging
text:
We are proposing to take advantage of recent developments in PET imaging technology and algorithms to
characterize, optimize, and harmonize cancer detection with PET imaging. This will use new artificial
intelligence methods and our recent technical developments to provide more accurate measurements and
phantoms for translation across multiple systems and imaging sites. This will lead to a roadmap for multi-site
and multi-vendor implementation approaches that improve early-stage cancer detection and diagnosis, and
thus improved patient outcomes.

title: Mechanisms of Impaired Granulopoiesis Due to CLPB Mutations
text:
Neutrophils are crucial immune system cells that act as a first line of defense against infections, and an
absence of neutrophils places patients at increased risk of death due to uncontrolled infection. We recently
identified a new genetic cause for severe congenital neutropenia (SCN), a rare disorder characterized by an
inability to generate mature, functional neutrophils. Studying the mechanisms underlying SCN will allow us to
make significant advances into basic neutrophil biology, leading to new therapies for SCN patients and patients
who have decreased neutrophil numbers in the setting of chemotherapy treatment.

title: Air pollution mixtures and pregnancy: assessing exposure, estimating risk, and predicting susceptibility with machine learning
text:
This study will determine the effect of exposure to mixtures of PM2.5, O3, NO2, and heat on placental
insufficiency during pregnancy using a causal random forest, which calculates weekly effect estimates with
confidence intervals. Population movement simulation models will be used to better estimate uncertainty in
exposure and its effects. The proposed research will improve our understanding of the effects of complex
mixtures of air pollutants on placental insufficiency using machine learning.

title: Rapid Species-Level Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring of NTM Infections Using a CRISPR-Droplet Platform
text:
Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) infections are increasing in prevalence, yet current diagnostic methods
rely on slow culture-based techniques, delaying timely treatment decisions. This project aims to develop and
clinically validate a CRISPR-Assisted, Nanodroplet-paired Differentiation test for NTM (CANDi-NTM)
for rapid, non-invasive NTM detection and drug resistance profiling, streamlining diagnosis and treatment
response monitoring. By integrating this innovative approach into clinical workflows, we seek to provide a
transformative tool for early and precise NTM management, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

title: Training Program in Patient-Oriented Research in Cardiovascular Endocrinology
text: The primary mission of this new Training Program is to train post-doctoral fellows in all aspects of patient-oriented research with a particular focus on the role of genetics, epigenetics, and endocrinology in the pathophysiology of cardiometabolic diseases. To accomplish this mission, the Program has recruited 16 outstanding primary mentors, each with a stellar record of NIH funding and excellence in mentorship evidenced by the high rates of retention of their trainees in academic research careers and by the success of their trainees in securing independent K series and/ or R series grants. The program, founded upon three core components - 1) a didactic learning core; 2) a mentored research project component; and 3) an individualized career development plan - is supported by an outstanding institutional research and education infrastructure and culture to accomplish its mission of nurturing the next generation of highly skilled academic investigators with expertise in patient-oriented research.

title: Project 2 - Uncovering Mechanisms of the Lymphoid Oncogenesis of Epstein-Barr Virus and Kaposi's Sarcoma
text:
PROJECT 2 − PROJECT NARRATIVE
Epstein-Barr Virus and Kaposi's Sarcoma Herpesvirus are human tumor viruses that cause lymphomas. We are
identifying how they cause Burkitt Lymphoma and Primary Effusion Lymphomas to foster development of
treatments for these cancers.

title: Statistical Framework for Unraveling Age-Dependent Genetic Landscape of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias: Harnessing Large-Scale EHR and DNA-Biobank Integration
text:
This project aims to build a more comprehensive understanding of the genetic architecture of Alzheimer's Disease
and related dementias, taking into account the complexities of age-related changes and diverse phenotypes.
By leveraging large-scale biobanks, electronic medical records, and innovative machine learning techniques,
we hope to uncover crucial insights that could lead to better understanding of disease progression, improved
prevention strategies and novel therapeutic targets, representing a signiﬁcant advancement in dementia research.

title: Automated Quality Evaluation and Harmonization for Multisite ASL MRI Data
text:
Arterial Spin Labeled perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (ASL-MRI) is the only non-invasive method to
measure regional cerebral blood flow and has been included as a part of multi-modal MRI in several multisite
longitudinal studies aimed at aging and Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) research. ASL data
can be noisy and can also vary significantly across sites. The proposed project will develop methods for
automated quality evaluation and harmonization of data that will ensure maximal data retainment, optimal
statistical analysis, and biomarker development.

title: Geometrical Regulation of Collective Cellular Responses in Three-Dimensional Space and Time
text:
Our research program investigates how macroscopic 3D tissue geometries—such as curvature, concavity, and
continuity—independently influence cell morphology, gene expression, and tissue homeostasis, focusing initially
on mesenchymal cells in skin and vascular tissues. By leveraging novel biofabrication and tissue engineering
techniques, we aim to systematically decouple and explore the effects of these geometric cues on cellular
behavior, both in steady-state and dynamically changing environments. Ultimately, this work may lead to new
therapeutic strategies targeting geometric regulation of cells and the development of more physiologically
relevant organ models, while also providing interdisciplinary training opportunities for future scientists and
clinicians.

title: Multilevel stress influences on longitudinal trajectories of tobacco use among young adults throughout the US
text: Our scientific premise leverages the socioecological framework and life course theory and builds on literature that indicates that: a) young adulthood is a time of increased risk of tobacco use initiation and escalation; b) young adults experiencing stress display greater risk of tobacco use; c) stress occurs across multiple levels and is influenced by the broader community environment; and d) a significant portion of young adults reside in areas with limited access to tobacco cessation programs. The overall goal of this research is to address knowledge gaps in prevention and cessation efforts targeting young adults by assessing longitudinal trajectories of tobacco use across a range of tobacco products, the multiple components of individual and interpersonal stress that may contribute to such use, and the bidirectional associations of stress and tobacco use among young adults living in areas with and without access to tobacco cessation programs.

title: A novel role of cholesterol and SR-BI in adipocyte biology
text:
The aim of the proposed research project is to determine how the HDL receptor SR-BI in
adipocytes regulates the process by which high-fat diet feeding induces lipid accumulation in
adipose tissue. We anticipate that the new knowledge gained will deepen our understanding of
adipocyte biology through investigation of a novel, previously unappreciated role of HDL-
cholesterol and its receptor SR-BI. Considering the staggering impact of obesity on metabolic
and cardiovascular diseases, the goal of the research project is in line with the objectives of the
National Institute of Health to address these disorders through medical research.

title: Targeting CD180 to induce anti-KSHV response in nonhuman primates
text:
Individuals with an underlying HIV-infection have an increased risk of developing AIDS-related malignancies.
Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) is the necessary causal agent for Kaposi's sarcoma and is a
cofactor in B cell lymphoproliferative disorders observed in AIDS patients. Devising a vaccine strategy that can
inhibit KSHV infection amongst the population is a necessary first step in creating a vaccine to prevent the spread
of KSHV worldwide and the results from the proposed studies utilizing the nonhuman primate model should help
elucidate and define vaccine strategies to prevent KSHV infection or KSHV-associated disease.

title: Development and characterization of self-amplifying RNA Lipid Nanoparticles for potent and multiplex gene expression in solid tumors
text:
This proposal describes the training and mentoring of Mr. Nambiar and his research project to further expand
and explore the applications of self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) for the treatment of solid tumors. He aims to
accomplish this both by optimizing nucleoside composition and lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vehicle properties, and
determining the maximum payload for saRNA (both in quantity of genes and total length of transgene). The
capability of these optimizations of the saRNA-LNP platform for allowing efficient and multiplex gene
expression in solid tumors will be assessed both in vitro and in vivo.
